sections.h2: Where is Farragut, Tennessee, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Farragut is a suburban town in Knox County with a small extension into Loudon County, part of the Knoxville metro area. The Town's own facts page gives its size as 16.2 square miles. Interstate 40/75 forms most of the northern edge, Turkey Creek Road and the Norfolk Southern rail line mark the south, the Loudon County line is the west boundary, and Lovell Road plus the Concord Hills subdivisions close off the east.

The 2020 census counted 23,506 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 25,121, a gain of 6.9 percent. Median age in 2020 was 46.7, and 23.7 percent of people were 65 or older. Married couples headed 70.8 percent of the 8,521 households. Of 8,992 housing units, 5.2 percent sat vacant, with a 1.5 percent vacancy rate among owner homes and 14.3 percent among rentals.

Those figures come from the census and the Town's facts page, and they are a useful backdrop for anyone weighing a sale of a Farragut house.

sections.h2: How did Farragut become a town?
sections.html:
The area began as Campbell's Station, a fort and stagecoach stop built by Captain David Campbell in 1787. The brick Campbell's Station Inn went up in 1810 and still stands on Kingston Pike within sight of Town Hall. The Battle of Campbell's Station was fought here on November 16, 1863. The town takes its name from Union Admiral David Farragut, who was born just east of here in 1801.

Incorporation came late. In December 1979 the Knoxville City Council voted to annex stretches of I-40 right-of-way in the Farragut area, and residents petitioned for an incorporation election. Farragut voted to incorporate on January 16, 1980, which blocked further annexation by Knoxville. Bob Leonard was elected the first mayor on April 1, 1980.

sections.h2: What does the land and climate mean for a Farragut house?
sections.html:
Farragut sits in hilly ground between Blackoak Ridge to the north and Fort Loudoun Lake on the Tennessee River to the south, at about 936 feet above sea level. Hills mean sloped lots, and sloped lots mean buyers and inspectors pay attention to drainage, retaining walls and foundations.

The Town reports these climate averages:

  • Annual precipitation of 47.86 inches and about 6 inches of snow
  • January highs near 46 degrees and July highs near 88
  • A freeze-free period averaging 214 days
  • Prevailing winds from the southwest

Nearly 48 inches of rain a year puts roofs, gutters and crawl spaces on every inspection list. A seller who has patched a leak or regraded a yard should keep the receipts for the buyer.

sections.h2: What does property tax look like for a Farragut homeowner?
sections.html:
Farragut levies no municipal property tax. Residents pay Knox County's rate of $1.55 per $100 of assessed value, and the Town reports that residential property is assessed at 25 percent of market value and commercial at 40 percent. Knox County sales tax is 9.25 percent, or 5.25 percent on groceries.

For a house valued at $600,000, the assessed value would be $150,000, and $1.55 per $100 yields $2,325 a year. That sum is an illustration built from the published rate, so check the actual bill on the trustee's site.

The Knox County Property Assessor reappraises on a two-year schedule and mails a notice whenever an assessed value changes. An owner who disagrees can appeal to the County Board of Equalization when it meets in June. The assessor also says that after a deed is recorded, its system can take up to a week to show the new owner.

sections.h2: Which permits and code rules affect a Farragut sale?
sections.html:
Farragut's Building and Fire Codes Division enforces the adopted building, plumbing, gas, mechanical, housing, swimming pool and fire codes. A permit is needed for most remodeling. Water heater change-outs, HVAC replacements and any gas appliance installation require permits and inspections through the Town, and mechanical applications must include a Manual J report. Electrical inspections run through the Lenoir City Utilities Board.

Work that skips a permit is the usual snag at closing, so it helps to confirm what was permitted before listing. Items on the Town's no-permit list include one-story detached sheds up to 200 square feet and fences up to 7 feet, though zoning approval may still apply.

Code enforcement follows a set path:

  • A complaint is reviewed and an officer does a drive-by inspection.
  • A courtesy notice goes to the owner, usually with a 10-day deadline, though it can range from immediate to 30 days.
  • If the problem persists, the owner can be cited to Municipal Court, where fines reach $50 per day per violation.
  • The Town may fix the problem itself and place a lien on the property for the cost.

A seller with an open notice should call Town Hall at 865-966-7057 before accepting any offer, because a lien would have to be dealt with at closing.

sections.h2: Which schools and roads shape demand in Farragut?
sections.html:
Most Farragut addresses are zoned to Knox County Schools: Farragut Primary (K-2), Farragut Intermediate (3-5), Farragut Middle (6-8) and Farragut High (9-12), with Northshore Elementary also serving the area. Part of the town north of I-75 is zoned for Hardin Valley Middle and Hardin Valley Academy. Knoxville Christian School and Concord Christian School are private options.

Kingston Pike, the merged US 70 and US 11, runs through the middle of town, and I-40/75 runs along its northern edge. The town lists commuting links to Oak Ridge, Knoxville, Maryville, Alcoa and McGhee Tyson Airport, and a commuter lot at Campbell Station Road and Campbell Lakes Drive serves ride sharers. Gas comes from the Knoxville Utilities Board, electricity from the Lenoir City Utility Board, and fire protection is subscription-based through Rural Metro.

A buyer who learns about the Rural Metro subscription early will not be surprised by it at closing.

sections.h2: How does a Farragut house sale move from offer to recorded deed?
sections.html:
An owner can list with an agent, sell directly to a buyer, or take a cash offer from a company that buys houses as-is. A cash sale suits a house that needs work, carries a code notice, or has a deadline attached. Whatever route is chosen, the deed is recorded in Knox County, not at Town Hall.

The Knox County Register of Deeds says a deed should be recorded as soon as possible, though no statutory time limit exists, and that signatures must be notarized or witnessed by two people. Documents are usually recorded the same day received. Tennessee's realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the purchase price, and the Department of Revenue says the grantee pays it when the deed is recorded.

The assessor will send a sales questionnaire after ownership changes, including a private sale or a transfer into a trust. Sellers should also tell the trustee where to mail later bills. Ask the Knox County Trustee how any current-year balance is handled at closing.

faqs.q: Does Farragut have its own property tax?
faqs.a: No. The Town of Farragut levies no municipal property tax, and residents pay the Knox County rate of $1.55 per $100 of assessed value. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of market value.

faqs.q: Where is a Farragut deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Knox County Register of Deeds in Suite 225 of the City County Building, 400 Main Street, Knoxville. Call 865-215-2330. Each county records only the real estate inside its own borders.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a water heater in Farragut?
faqs.a: Yes. The Town of Farragut requires a permit and inspection for water heater change-outs, HVAC replacements and gas appliance installations. Contact the Codes office at 865-966-7057 or 865-675-2384 if you are unsure.

faqs.q: What happens if Farragut sends me a code courtesy notice before I sell?
faqs.a: Respond before the deadline, usually 10 days. If the issue is still open at the follow-up inspection, the owner can be cited to Municipal Court, with fines up to $50 per day per violation, and the Town can place a lien after fixing the problem.

faqs.q: Who is the transfer tax paid by on a Farragut sale?
faqs.a: The buyer, as grantee. Tennessee charges $0.37 per $100 of purchase price when the deed is recorded, and the Register of Deeds collects it for the Department of Revenue.
